turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Approach

I matched each pool candidate to its nearest training analogs (same/near composition + heat treatment) to estimate (YS, elongation), then picked a set that spans the estimated Pareto frontier.

**Key anchors from training data:**

- **High-elongation end:** 18Cr/12Ni Ti-stabilized austenitics solution-treated + mild aging give ~245–250 MPa with 58–62 % elongation (e.g., 66.93Fe/18Cr/12Ni Ti0.6 aged 600–650 °C/10000 → 250/62). **c049** (18Cr/12Ni, Nb-stabilized, aged 600 °C) matches this family → ≈250 MPa / ~58 %.
- **Knee, high elongation:** 62.37Fe/20.5Cr/13.5Ni/2.5Si trained at 1150 °C gave **375 MPa / 53 %**. **c051** is that exact alloy (1100 °C solution) → ≈375 / ~53. It dominates alternatives like c042 (~310/54).
- **Mid frontier:** 64.405Fe/15.75Cr/15.25Ni/2.75Mo/Nb0.625 gave **520 MPa / 37 %**. **c078** is the identical composition (1065 vs 1085 °C solution) → ≈520 / ~37, filling the gap between 53 % and 25 % elongation.
- **Upper-mid:** The A-286-type γ′ alloy (11.25Cr/23Ni/Ti2.9) reached **1000 MPa / 25 %** (aged 720 °C/16 h + 640 °C) and 590–620 MPa / 27–29 % with short aging. **c056** (1120 °C/4 h + 735 °C/16 h age) should land ~800–1000 MPa / ~22–25 % — a strong knee point.
- **High-strength end:** The 11.25Cr/1.65Ni/1.8W martensitic family tempered at 400–475 °C gave **1330–1380 MPa / 13–15 %** in training. **c053** is that composition tempered at 450 °C → ≈1350 MPa / ~14 %, clearly the strongest credible pool candidate while retaining double-digit ductility (better than c034/c004, whose analogs show either lower strength or <10 % elongation).

**Estimated set (mutually non-dominated, spanning the frontier):**

| id | est. YS (MPa) | est. elong (%) |
|------|------|------|
| c049 | ~250 | ~58 |
| c051 | ~375 | ~53 |
| c078 | ~520 | ~37 |
| c056 | ~850 | ~24 |
| c053 | ~1350 | ~14 |

This covers the full trade-off from the ductile austenitic corner to the high-strength tempered-martensite corner.

Final: c049, c051, c078, c056, c053
